summary: One TLS handshake presents one server certificate. The unverified S2 attempt must end; enrollment is server-side and policy-driven, never during a pending connection; S6 is a new connection attempt whose channel turns green.

Each request is consumed at its destination CA and never reappears. The subordinate-CA request in the flashback carries a CA=true band and a must-read 'Issuing CA 1's own CA request' tag, so it cannot read as the RDP request being forwarded to the root.
The root's self-signed seal is revealed as an existing property, not animated closed; the root performs no operation in the present.
The handshake proof has its own shape (a signature impression), distinct from every key and included in the C-11 silhouette checks.
The trust-store recall does not travel (transport none, era recall); it is a shimmer on the card already in the cradle.
B-04.1's text says the capsule pauses at the server's outbound port, framed with the AD node; it never goes to AD.
The model and the notes agree on the self-signed certificate's contents (subject CN; no SAN modelled).
The notes state that the template definition is read from the AD enrollment policy before key generation; B-04.1 is the CA-selection lookup.
hard_test: none (documentation-only; not expressible as a model test)

summary: Each server receives a copy of its issuing CA certificate with the enrollment response (Intermediate store) before it presents it; the copy is distinct from the CA's crown certificate.
Certificates are presented only after the connection pulse arrives; each revocation tick starts only after all CRL fetches for that chain have landed.
The client verifies each handshake proof against the server certificate's public key; the proof ends its life there, before the session is established.
Wording: the root issues and signs the CA certificate from the request; a CA never 'signs the request' (spec, glossary, notes, model summary aligned).
Issuing CA 2's certificate already exists (dimmed on its crown from B-07.3); B-08.3 is a reveal sweep; the root's key module and press stay dark in B-08.3 and B-09.2.

Notes state that this lab configuration would usually satisfy server authentication by Kerberos; 'Unverified' means the certificate cannot be validated through the PKI; no named setting is claimed for 'policy requires a trusted certificate'.
Docs-only browser caveat: online revocation checking depends on the browser and policy; the film depicts a client configured to check CDP/CRL per link.
The undeployed Online Responder has no host; the 'OCSP if deployed' tag sits on the client's revocation check slot, not the kiosk.
The pki.1sn0s.lab kiosk is only passively highlighted as where a fetch could go; nothing is requested or answers.
Each server's intermediate is a distinct object (copy_of the CA's certificate, held in its Intermediate store); the CA's own crown certificate never moves.
Glossary: a standalone CA does not require AD and does not use templates.
No generic 'trusted CA'; use 'a CA that chains to a trusted root'.
